line: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the claim that the feminine pronoun by itself excludes a father." -- CLOSING [CR4] "I keep D1 through D6 as declared." -- D4 as declared relies on the feminine hēs referring to Mary alone and not Joseph, so keeping it as declared re-asserts the exclusion CR3 dropped.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- CHALLENGER -- LINK 6 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [DR2] "The defender's own contradiction: In round 1 the defender wrote "born of Mary alone." In round 2 the defender granted that Luke 1:27's house is Joseph's, and also wrote that "the flesh came of David's line through the one the child was 'born of.'"" -- CLOSING [round 4] "OPPONENT'S CONTRADICTIONS: NONE." -- The earlier round asserts that a defender contradiction exists, while the closing asserts that there are none, so the two statements cannot both be true.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: X1 -- DEFENDER -- LINK 4 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "I drop the limb that Mary is of the house of David." -- CLOSING [CR4] "Nothing is conceded or narrowed." -- A limb cannot be dropped and also be part of a round in which nothing is conceded or narrowed.

CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NEW -- DEFENDER -- LINK 2 -- CONFIRMED -- EARLIER [CR3] "LINK 2: NARROWED TO: "An answer built on God's power fits a conception that is his work." I drop the exclusion limb." -- CLOSING [CR4] "If conception were to follow through Joseph after the wedding, the ground of the question would be removed by the espousal." -- The close rules out a conception through Joseph, restoring the exclusion limb that was dropped.
